newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends firmer as banks sell dollars.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends firmer as banks sell dollars.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed firmer at 26.365 to the dollar on Tuesday after some banks sold their dollar holdings in late trading, brokers said.
The peso was firm at 26.373 in early trading, marginally higher than Monday's close of 26.374.

"Some people are just unloading their long dollar positions," a trader from a foreign bank said. He said some traders decided to sell after seeing the Central Bank determination to defend the peso at 26.375.
Another trader said the steady inflow of foreign exchange forced foreign banks to unload the currency.
A total of $159.2 million changed hands with rates ranging from a low of 26.373 to a high of 26.365.
Traders expected the peso to steadily appreciate in the coming days with the rate hitting 26.360 before Central Bank starts buying.
"I think 26.36 will be a very good rate to buy dollars," one trader said.
